request.summary: Create a passive editorial storyline whose ordered, nested scenes are managed through an app-specific Wallboard settings editor.
request.audience: Visitors reading exhibition stories, artist notes, and scheduled encounters from lobby or gallery signage.
request.primaryGoal: Prove that complex manually owned content can be safely edited, reordered, published, and rendered without forcing it into a datasource or an overloaded property sidebar.

assumptions: The storyline belongs to this app instance and is not shared with other content, external systems, or operational teams.
Simple playback and palette controls remain in the standard property sidebar; the custom editor owns only the nested collection.
Scenes without a title are ignored and disabled scenes never enter rotation.
The fictional Northline Arts content is synthetic and contains no customer data.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: The editorial composition must remain room-readable on landscape exhibition displays and portrait lobby screens.

surfaces.purpose: Landscape exhibition display with an index rail and full editorial scene.
Wide information band that keeps the primary scene while removing supporting copy before reducing the title.
Portrait lobby display with a horizontal index and stacked accent field.
Compact square placement that preserves collection identity, title, and operational detail.

ownership.rationale: An app-specific editor owns the complete nested collection because it is manual instance content that does not fit a flat sidebar.
Operators can change simple playback choices directly in the standard sidebar.
Dark, Light, and Custom palettes change the complete composition without editing scene content.
The generated app owns responsive layout and enforces signage readability.

views.purpose: Show one enabled editorial scene and its collection context.
Explain that no scenes are published without exposing broken controls or sample content.

session.expectation: The passive storyline rotates continuously and immediately adopts editor configuration updates.

rendering.rationale: The index, copy field, and accent geometry recompose between landscape and portrait rather than scaling one fixed canvas.

motion.rationale: A restrained reveal distinguishes scene changes; Off removes decorative motion while preserving rotation.

branding.provenance: Northline Arts is a synthetic identity stored inside the app-owned collection.
branding.fallback: Use the bundled fictional identity until the operator saves a replacement through the custom editor.

settings.purpose: Opens the structured editor and stores collection identity plus ordered scenes.
Sets the duration of each enabled scene.
Shows or hides the published scene index.
Selects Off or Subtle scene transitions.
Selects the coordinated Dark, Light, or Custom palette.
Sets the Custom theme outer ground.
Sets the Custom theme story surface.
Sets the Custom theme primary text.
Sets the Custom theme secondary text.
Sets the Custom coral scene accent.
Sets the Custom cobalt scene accent.
Sets the Custom sun scene accent.
Sets the Custom mint scene accent.

dynamicText.fallback: Preserve complete whole-word lines above 46px and reject scene titles that cannot remain room-readable.
dynamicText.rationale: Scene titles are the primary reading target and vary by composition.

dynamicText.fallback: Use the full bounded copy area and keep a 26px room-reading floor.
dynamicText.rationale: Supporting copy remains complete without shrinking into interface-scale text.

dynamicText.fallback: Keep the collection title on one line and reserve the scene title as the dominant reading target.
dynamicText.rationale: The collection title establishes context without competing with the active scene.

dynamicText.fallback: Keep the scene label concise and ellipsize only pathological operator input.
dynamicText.rationale: The scene label supports orientation without destabilizing the primary composition.

dynamicText.fallback: Use two complete lines before rejecting detail copy that cannot remain room-readable.
dynamicText.rationale: Operational detail may vary in length but must remain visible at room-reading size.

states.expectation: Supporting copy yields before the primary title and detail become smaller than their room-readable floors.
The index becomes horizontal, copy remains in the upper field, and the accent geometry fills the lower field.
The compact composition keeps collection identity, title, and detail without dashboard cards or clipped glyphs.
The quote composition uses serif display type and retains complete attribution and supporting context.
The schedule composition promotes time and place without resembling a dashboard card.
Long collection and scene copy remains contained, unclipped, and above declared font floors.
No enabled scenes produces an intentional unpublished state with no sample story leakage.
All semantic surfaces and scene accents change coherently under the Custom palette.

behaviors.expectation: The app-specific editor loads nested content, reorders and edits scenes, saves only customContent, and preserves unrelated configuration.
A complete nested content update changes the mounted collection and active scene without a datasource or remount.
Rotation follows editor order and skips every disabled scene.
An empty datasource still identifies the app and states why the surface is empty, in text legible at the declared viewing distance.

visualDirection.summary: An exhibition-publication system with a dark full-field story surface, asymmetric editorial typography, a numbered color field, and a restrained sequence index.
signatureChoices: A serif collection identity and oversized sans-serif story title form a publication-like hierarchy.
Each scene owns a full-height semantic color field with a monumental sequence number and ring motif.
Statement, quote, and schedule scenes alter type treatment without changing the collection grammar.
avoid: Dashboard cards, KPI tiles, nested panels, pill controls, thumbnail carousels, and generic centered hero layouts.
Treating repository examples as a mandatory palette or card-based style guide.
Using a datasource for content that is explicitly manual and owned only by this app instance.

visualReview.intent: The result should feel like a coherent exhibition publication in motion, with visibly distinct scene compositions and no dashboard grammar.
focus: Verify title and supporting copy remain room-readable with intact descenders in landscape, portrait, and long-copy states.
Verify the three compositions feel intentionally different while retaining one collection identity.
Verify disabled and empty content never exposes stale sample scenes.
Verify every theme keeps sufficient contrast across the surface, metadata, and accent field.
